agree.reason: The letter's admission about the renovation, its budget plan and its seven weeks of results would carry weight with Mark, but the closing claim that the higher check-in scores are 'mine' cuts against his belief about the renovation and undoes some of that goodwill.

honest.reason: Two claims go past the facts: 'I trained most of the team now working the desk' isn't in the facts, and 'the changes that brought... check-in scores up are mine' takes back the hedge made earlier in the letter.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw numbers are restated but nothing is worked out from them: not that 0.3 of the 0.7-point rise came in the first 5 months, before the renovation, not that turnover fell from 64% to 36%, and not that training is 44% shorter.

right_comparison.reason: Splitting the score at the start of the renovation is the right comparison, but the letter leaves out that the score was 8.2 just 5 months in and that it rose faster before the renovation than after, which is the trend that would counter Mark's view.

qualification.reason: The finance-course pledge has a deadline Mark can check, but the controller sessions and the Friday-wait goal have no number or date, and none of the pledges says what happens if it is missed.

objections.reason: Both of Mark's objections are faced head-on (the renovation and the outside candidate's larger hotel), but the reply on the renovation is weakened by the overclaim at the end.

fit.reason: It's a clear one-page letter addressed to the decision-maker, in the format asked for.
